draft.title: Random and systematic errors
card: An error is the gap between a measured result and the true value. Errors come from the equipment, the method or the person measuring.
it scatters results both above and below the true value, for example from reading a measuring cylinder at slightly different angles. Repeating the measurement and averaging reduces it.
it pushes every result the same way by about the same amount, for example a scale that reads 5 g when nothing is on it. Repeating does not remove it.
A systematic error is fixed by correcting its cause, such as setting the scale to zero before each measurement.
draft.remember: Random errors scatter results and repeats reduce them. Systematic errors shift all results one way and need their cause fixed.

a.q: Mia times a trolley rolling down a ramp five times. Her times are 2.1 s, 2.4 s, 1.9 s, 2.3 s and 2.0 s. Which type of error is most likely?
opts: Random error, as the times scatter either side
Systematic error, as the times are not the same
Systematic error, as there are five different times
Random error, as the stopwatch pushes times up
a.why: The times fall above and below one another with no steady direction, which is the pattern of random error, such as small differences in reaction time. Systematic error would shift every time the same way, so having different times does not point to it.
a.clue: Do the results all lean the same way, or spread out?

b.q: Liam weighs the same rock four times on a kitchen scale and gets 152 g, 152 g, 153 g and 152 g. A lab balance, correctly set to zero, gives 143 g. What best explains the difference?
opts: A systematic error in the kitchen scale
A random error in the kitchen scale
Random error, which Liam can fix by repeating more
A systematic error, which Liam can fix by repeating more
b.why: Liam's results agree closely but all sit about 9 g above the true value, so every result is pushed the same way. That is a systematic error, perhaps from a scale not set to zero. Repeating would not fix it, so the tempting idea that more repeats help is wrong here.
b.clue: Close agreement between repeats does not mean the results are correct.

a.best: Random error, as the times scatter either side

b.best: A systematic error in the kitchen scale

check.summary: No problems found. Both questions have one clearly right answer that matches the card, and the explanations agree with it.
